content_metadata.description: A conversation between an interviewer and interviewee discussing the continuous nature of evolution and adaptation in response to environmental changes.

characterInteraction.description: The two men engage in a lively and friendly discussion with mutual respect and understanding.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The conversation delves into the ongoing nature of evolution and adaptation, particularly in response to technological and societal changes.

narrativeProgression.description: The Interviewer asks about evolution happening now.
The Interviewee explains that evolution is continuous for everything.
The Interviewer jokes that this sounds complicated.
The Interviewee agrees and mentions adaptive modification.
The Interviewee notes that humans are the only species with a long maturation period.
The Interviewee talks about adapting to new environments.
The Interviewee explains that moving to a new place requires readaptation.
The Interviewee discusses how even if you don't move, your environment changes.
The Interviewer mentions the rapid changes in the modern world.
The Interviewee brings up the example of Google's Go program.
The Interviewee talks about accessing information differently than in the past.
The Interviewer talks about recognizing the provisional nature of identities.
The Interviewer mentions how it feels terrible to be discrete.
The Interviewee states there is no fixed identity.
The Interviewer suggests that we are not things, but dynamically evolving.
The Interviewee agrees and says that this feels better.

climax.description: Recognition of evolving identities beyond fixed notions.

youtube_description:
Rich Doyle and Gary Weber in Dialogue on the continuing evolution of everything, including our operating system as our environment changes.  Why our maturation is delayed to allow our species to  survive in any environment.   The application of adaptive learning in changing environments to continuing, critical modifications of the "I" software program.  

The two blogposts mentioned are: a) "Why we're 'complicated' from 12 to 30...recent research" @ http://happinessbeyondthought.blogspot.com/2015/05/why-were-complicated-from-12-to.html, and
